browser.title: Project Reference Index
browser.intro: Notes on papers, sourcebooks, and implementation dependencies connected to the projects. These sources provide context; the project evidence remains in the code, prototypes, and results.

references.title: A New Solution to the Random Assignment Problem
references.citation: Anna Bogomolnaia and Hervé Moulin · Journal of Economic Theory 100(2)
references.summary: Introduces Probabilistic Serial as a random-assignment mechanism and makes its trade-offs explicit: ordinal efficiency and envy-freeness improve, while strategy-proofness does not survive.
references.annotation: This reference informed the project's simultaneous-eating stage and clarified the mechanism-level tradeoffs behind probabilistic assignment.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: A Solution to the Random Assignment Problem on the Full Preference Domain
references.citation: Akshay-Kumar Katta and Jay Sethuraman · Journal of Economic Theory 131(1)
references.summary: Extends random assignment beyond strict rankings by allowing indifference between objects, reinterpreting Probabilistic Serial as an iterative network-flow problem.
references.annotation: This reference extends the project's theoretical foundation beyond strict preference rankings by considering cases in which participants may be indifferent between options.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: Simultaneously Achieving Ex-Ante and Ex-Post Fairness
references.citation: Haris Aziz · Web and Internet Economics, LNCS 12495 · pp. 341–355
references.summary: Connects fairness before a lottery is resolved with fairness in the deterministic allocations produced afterward, including an implementation of the Probabilistic Serial outcome through ex-post EF1 allocations.
references.annotation: This reference supplied part of the original project's fairness lineage. It does not establish that the implementation reproduced the paper's complete formal mechanism.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: The Vigilant Eating Rule: A General Approach for Probabilistic Economic Design with Constraints
references.citation: Haris Aziz and Florian Brandl · Games and Economic Behavior 135 · pp. 168–187
references.summary: Develops an eating-rule mechanism for probabilistic allocation under broad feasibility constraints, with attention to constrained efficiency and equal treatment.
references.annotation: This source contextualized the project's simultaneous-eating approach and its possible extension to constrained allocation; it is retained as historical background rather than an implementation claim.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: Random Serial Dictatorship and the Core from Random Endowments in House Allocation Problems
references.citation: Atila Abdulkadiroğlu and Tayfun Sönmez · Econometrica 66(3) · pp. 689–701
references.summary: Studies Random Serial Dictatorship in house-allocation problems and provides an alternative random-assignment lineage against which probabilistic mechanisms can be considered.
references.annotation: The original presentation used this reference as an alternative random-assignment mechanism. The current code should not be described as implementing the paper's full model without further evidence.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: Three Observations on Linear Algebra
references.citation: Garrett Birkhoff · Universidad Nacional de Tucumán, Revista A 5
references.summary: The decomposition result behind converting a fractional allocation matrix into a weighted collection of deterministic assignments.
references.annotation: In the project, decomposition is the bridge between an abstract fractional result and a lottery over assignments that can actually be issued to students.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: Matching Theory
references.citation: László Lovász and Michael D. Plummer · Annals of Discrete Mathematics 29 · North-Holland
references.summary: A foundational treatment of matching, network flows, matching algorithms, and the linear-programming structures that support assignment problems.
references.annotation: This book belongs to the original project's mathematical foundation. It supports the assignment and decomposition context without implying that every algorithm in the volume was implemented.
references.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

references.title: Using an Electromyogram Technique to Detect Muscle Activity
references.citation: Sylvain Colliard-Piraud · STMicroelectronics Application Note AN4995
references.summary: Explains a surface-EMG acquisition chain from three skin electrodes through differential amplification, rectification, low-pass filtering, and a comparator or microcontroller input.
references.annotation: This reference supports the project's sensing and conditioning context. Its example circuit is background material, not a claim that the wearable reproduces the complete ST design.

references.title: Integrating Health in Urban and Territorial Planning
references.citation: World Health Organization and UN-Habitat · Sourcebook
references.summary: Connects planning decisions with transport, housing, food, education, healthcare, environment, well-being, and health equity rather than reducing urban quality of life to one indicator.
references.annotation: The Shanghai project followed a smaller, local version of this logic: ask residents what matters, then translate nearby services and walking time into something visible.
references.provenance: BACKGROUND READING / NOT CLAIMED AS AN ORIGINAL PROJECT SOURCE

references.title: Frequency Analysis of the Surface EMG Signal: Best Practices
references.citation: Silvia Muceli and Roberto Merletti · Journal of Electromyography and Kinesiology 79 · 102937
references.summary: Reviews time- and frequency-domain descriptions of surface EMG, including sampling, filtering, spectra, stationarity, epoch selection, coherence, and fatigue indices.
references.annotation: This reference complements the hardware-oriented application note with analysis guardrails. It informs future signal interpretation without claiming that the current prototype already performs frequency-based fatigue analysis.
